metadata.description: Azure region to deploy into. Defaults to Australia East; change it to deploy elsewhere.

DNS label for the free <label>.<region>.cloudapp.azure.com hostname. Must be globally unique within the region. Defaults to a generated value so a one-click deploy doesn't require inventing a globally-unique name.
Custom domain (e.g. patchpilot.yourdomain.com). Leave blank to use the free cloudapp.azure.com hostname instead. You can switch later without redeploying.
Admin username for the VM (used only for break-glass SSH access).
Enable inbound SSH (port 22) for break-glass access. PatchPilot never needs SSH for setup or day-to-day operation (az vm run-command is used instead) — leave this off to shrink the deploy form.

SSH public key content for the admin user. Always required by the VM resource (Azure Linux VMs need a credential even with password auth disabled), but network-unreachable unless enableSsh is true. Defaults to a placeholder key with no known private key anywhere — safe only because enableSsh defaults to false (no NSG rule opens port 22, so the key can never actually be used). If you set enableSsh to true, you MUST override this with your own public key or the VM will be unreachable via SSH — the placeholder locks you out, it does not grant anyone access.
CIDR allowed to reach SSH (22) when enableSsh is true, e.g. "1.2.3.4/32". Use "*" to allow any source (not recommended). Ignored when enableSsh is false.
VM size. Standard_B2as_v2 (2 vCPU/8GB) is comfortable for the full stack with AI features off. Use Standard_B4as_v2 (4 vCPU/16GB) if you plan to enable local AI (Ollama + llama3.1:8b).
Git repository URL to clone onto the VM. Point this at your own fork to deploy custom code instead of upstream mkheagerty-lab/PatchPilot.
Git branch or tag to check out after cloning repoUrl.

variables.cloudInitRaw:
#cloud-config # Boot-time provisioning for the PatchPilot Azure VM. Deployed via main.bicep, # which substitutes __PP_DOMAIN__, __ADMIN_USER__, __REPO_URL__, and __REPO_REF__ # before base64-encoding this file into the VM's customData. Everything below # runs once, automatically, on first boot — no SSH session required to bring # the stack up. package_update: true package_upgrade: true packages: - git - unattended-upgrades - ca-certificates - curl # Boot-time placeholder so https://$DOMAIN answers something immediately # instead of a dead connection for the ~10 minutes the real stack takes to # build — see the pp-placeholder container started below. write_files: - path: /opt/patchpilot-placeholder/index.html permissions: '0644' content: | PatchPilot is deploying…

PatchPilot is deploying…

This typically takes about 10 minutes. This page refreshes automatically — no action needed.

runcmd: # Keep the OS patched without anyone logging in. - systemctl enable --now unattended-upgrades # Docker's official convenience script installs docker-ce + the `docker # compose` v2 CLI plugin together — more reliable than Ubuntu's own apt # package names, which vary by release. - curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh - usermod -aG docker __ADMIN_USER__ - systemctl enable --now docker # Boot-time placeholder so something answers HTTPS immediately — the real # Caddy/Compose stack isn't up for ~10 more minutes. Shares the named # volumes the real `caddy` Compose service (project name "patchpilot", see # docker-compose.yml) will use, so the cert issued here is reused rather # than re-requested once the real stack takes over. - | docker run -d --name pp-placeholder --restart unless-stopped \ -p 80:80 -p 443:443 \ -v patchpilot_caddy_data:/data \ -v patchpilot_caddy_config:/config \ -v /opt/patchpilot-placeholder:/srv/pp-placeholder:ro \ caddy:2.11-alpine \ caddy file-server --domain __PP_DOMAIN__ --root /srv/pp-placeholder - git clone --branch __REPO_REF__ --single-branch __REPO_URL__ /opt/patchpilot - cp /opt/patchpilot/.env.example /opt/patchpilot/.env # Fill in the domain (auto cloudapp.azure.com hostname or a custom domain, # resolved by main.bicep before this file is templated) and generate fresh # secrets locally on the VM — nothing secret ever passes through the Azure # deployment template or its logs. - | DOMAIN="__PP_DOMAIN__" SESSION_SECRET=$(openssl rand -base64 32) TOKEN_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 32) PG_PASS=$(openssl rand -base64 24 | tr -d '/+=') ENV_FILE=/opt/patchpilot/.env sed -i "s#^PUBLIC_URL=.*#PUBLIC_URL=https://${DOMAIN}#" "$ENV_FILE" sed -i "s#^PP_DOMAIN=.*#PP_DOMAIN=${DOMAIN}#" "$ENV_FILE" sed -i "s#^AUTH_REDIRECT_URI=.*#AUTH_REDIRECT_URI=https://${DOMAIN}/auth/callback#" "$ENV_FILE" sed -i "s#^CORS_ORIGINS=.*#CORS_ORIGINS=https://${DOMAIN}#" "$ENV_FILE" sed -i "s#^SESSION_SECRET=.*#SESSION_SECRET=${SESSION_SECRET}#" "$ENV_FILE" sed -i "s#^TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY=.*#TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY=${TOKEN_KEY}#" "$ENV_FILE" sed -i "s#^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=.*#POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${PG_PASS}#" "$ENV_FILE" sed -i "s#^DATABASE_URL=.*#DATABASE_URL=postgres://patchpilot:${PG_PASS}@postgres:5432/patchpilot#" "$ENV_FILE" sed -i "s#^DEMO_MODE=.*#DEMO_MODE=false#" "$ENV_FILE" # ENTRA_* stays at its placeholder value on purpose — the app boots with # no Entra credentials and serves the "Pair this instance" setup screen # until the phone-home pairing flow (Deploy-PatchPilot.ps1) supplies them. # Compose brings up postgres/redis/ollama, waits for the one-shot `migrate` # container to apply pending Drizzle migrations, then starts api/worker/web/ # caddy/backup. Caddy requests its Let's Encrypt certificate for $DOMAIN on # first request. AI features stay off (AI_FEATURES_ENABLED=false, the # .env.example default) — ollama still runs (api/worker depend on it being # healthy) but no model is pulled, so it stays idle and cheap. # # --env-file .env is required here: Compose resolves its own ${VAR} # interpolation (used directly in this file's `environment:` blocks, e.g. # postgres's POSTGRES_PASSWORD) against a .env file next to the compose # file (infra/.env) by default, not the caller's cwd — but the real # generated secrets above were written to /opt/patchpilot/.env (repo # root). Without this flag every such variable silently resolves to a # blank string instead of erroring, so postgres starts with no password # and fails its healthcheck. This is separate from (and in addition to) # each service's own `env_file: ../.env`, which only injects vars into # the container's runtime environment and does not affect this # file-level interpolation. # Free ports 80/443 before the real Caddy binds them. - docker stop pp-placeholder && docker rm pp-placeholder - cd /opt/patchpilot && docker compose -f infra/docker-compose.yml --env-file .env up -d --build

source.script:
#!/bin/bash
        set -uo pipefail
        cloud-init status --wait
        timeout_s=1500
        elapsed=0
        until curl -fsS -o /dev/null http://localhost/api/health; do
          if [ "$elapsed" -ge "$timeout_s" ]; then
            echo "PatchPilot did not become ready within ${timeout_s}s" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          sleep 10
          elapsed=$((elapsed + 10))
        done
        echo "PatchPilot is ready."
